function: Over-the-air aggregation of local model updates, first from mobile users to intermediate servers (cluster aggregation) and then from servers to the parameter server (global aggregation) (pp. 6-9).
system: Single-antenna MUs (20) and ISs (4) transmit; each IS and the PS has 100 receive antennas; no RIS; frequency band not stated (pp. 6, 13).
method: Federated learning of a single-layer network (MNIST) and a CNN (CIFAR-10), supervised classification, Adam optimizer; hierarchical uncoded analog OTA aggregation (pp. 5-7, 13).
data_channel: Simulated Rayleigh small-scale fading with path loss d^-p, p = 4; MNIST and CIFAR-10 for the learning task; no standardized or measured channel (pp. 7, 13).
test_conditions: Settings: i.i.d., non-i.i.d. users, non-i.i.d. clusters; I = 1, 2, 4; tau = 1, 3, 5; same fading statistics, noise and power schedule in each run (pp. 13-15).
baselines: Conventional OTA FL (all users send directly to the PS, no ISs) and ideal error-free-link FL benchmarks; no non-learned method or cited prior design (pp. 4, 14).
metrics: Test accuracy versus total iterations (Figs. 2-3), average transmit power at the edge, and numerical convergence-rate upper bound on the loss (Fig. 4) (pp. 14-15).
complexity: none beyond model size: 2N = 7850 (MNIST) and 307498 (CIFAR-10); no aggregation cost, FLOPs, or runtime (p. 13).
openness: none; MNIST and CIFAR-10 are cited public learning datasets, no code or channel data link given (pp. 13, 30).
q1_support: p. 7: "small-scale fading coefficient (i.e., Rayleigh fading)" - custom Rayleigh model with distance path loss; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 14: "The experiments are performed with two different data distributions." - each setting is a separate run; no model is trained in one condition and tested in another.
q3_support: p. 14: "the conventional FL scheme, i.e., I = 1, with no IS in-between" - compared only with this variant and error-free ideal baselines; no non-learned method, no cited prior design.
q4_support: p. 13: "784 input neurons and 10 output neurons with 2N = 7850" - only the model size is given; no complexity order, operations or runtime of the aggregation.
q5_support: p. 13: "we use two different image classification datasets, MNIST" - learning-task datasets only; the channel is simulated and no code or data link is given.
notes: PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (2207.09232v1, 19 Jul 2022; p. 1). Area 7: the problem solved is OTA aggregation in hierarchical FL (Sec. III-B, p. 6). Receivers have 100 antennas (p. 13), so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply.
